ir.note: Schiit ship ONE remote for the whole preamp line: "It's the same one we use for all Sagas, Freyas, and Kara" (Saga 2 manual, Remote Control). So a frame meant for one of them reaches every other one in the room, and each unit needs its own emitter over its IR window rather than a shared blaster. Schiit do not publish the codes themselves — the manuals document the five buttons (Input, Volume Up, Volume Down, Output, Mute) and nothing about protocol or values — so commands here have to be captured from the physical remote. Protocol and address are a hardware capture, not a Schiit document: read off the supplied remote on 2026-09-08 with a USB IR Toy v2 on /dev/lirc0 (scripts/link/ir-capture.py, raw log in data/ir-captures/). Extended NEC, 16-bit address 0x1BF1, five distinct commands 0xF1-0xF5 — one per button, which matches the five buttons the manuals describe. Because every Saga, Freya and Kara answers this one remote, a frame reaches all of them: fit an emitter over each unit's window rather than using a shared blaster. 38 kHz is the NEC nominal carrier, not a measured value.

sources: hardware capture, Schiit preamp remote, USB IR Toy v2, 2026-09-08
metadata.notes: Original Saga: passive or tube-buffered preamp with a relay stepped attenuator. Schiit no longer publish its manual; the remote citation is the Saga 2 manual. Icon: the generic amplifier chassis, not a Schiit fascia. This library's glyphs are pixel-measured off a straight-on front elevation, and Schiit publish only three-quarter renders (freyaplus-LISST-front-1920.jpg, kara-front-blk-1920.jpg are both in perspective), so a measured Freya/Saga/Kara fascia is still owed a square-on photograph.
